blocks.text: Group is a logical entity that includes several users. Creating user groups helps in assigning multiple users to the Zscaler services quickly. You can create user groups to categorize users for various services and assign these user groups to administrative entitlements, service entitlements, admin roles, etc. You can create custom groups and use the predefined groups for a set of users.

If your organization uses Unified Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), administrator roles for Authentication Service and some Zscaler services are managed on a different Role Management page. To learn more, see About Role Management. Unified RBAC is a feature in limited availability. To access Unified RBAC, contact your Zscaler Account team.

blocks.item: Dynamic Group Administrators: User group with administrative entitlements.
Zscaler Global Administrators: Initial user group with global administrative entitlements.
Zscaler Emergency Access: User group that has Private Access (ZPA) emergency access entitlement.
Dynamic Group Guest Domains: Group of users from guest domains.
Dynamic Group Registered Domains: Group of users from registered domains.

blocks.text: User groups provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Provide a quick and simple way to assign multiple users to a Zscaler service in one attempt.
Categorize users into groups based on their admin roles, administrative access, service access, etc.

blocks.text: A user can be part of up to 1,000 groups. You must have similar limits on the respective services to support the 1,000 group assignments per user. If you don't have enough limits on the service side, the respective service considers group assignments up to the service limit for a user. For example, if you assign a user to 500 groups, but you have a Private Access service subscription for only 128 groups per user, then only the first 128 group assignment for the user is considered on the Private Access service.
On the User Groups page (Administration > Authentication > User Groups), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Click the Filter icon to display the search options. You can search for a group by group name or username.
Reset the page to the default view.
Import new user group, or modify existing user group, using a CSV file.
Add a user group.
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
Bulk delete user groups. This option is visible only when you select more than one user group.
View a list of configured user groups. For each user group, you can see:
Name: The name of the user group.
Users: The number of users in a group.
Description: A short description about the user group.
Select groups to perform bulk deletions. Select more than one user group to view the Delete option.
Edit or delete a group.
You cannot edit or delete predefined groups.
View the predefined group details. Click the Users tab to view a list of users in a group.
